message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Understanding the semantics of program code is a fundamental problem in software engineering, posing continuous challenges for testing and analysis, as well as for AI agents. We introduce
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">neural program modeling</jats:italic>
                    : an approach that
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">learns</jats:italic>
                    the relationship between
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">input features</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">execution features</jats:italic>
                    (such as traces or coverage) from pairs of generated system inputs and monitored execution data. The resulting
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">program-specific model</jats:italic>
                    can
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">predict system inputs</jats:italic>
                    that trigger desired program behaviors—in seconds, without executing the program. It can also
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">predict program traces and coverage</jats:italic>
                    for a given input, again without running the program.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    Once trained, such a model acts as a
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">proxy</jats:italic>
                    for the program under test, supporting a range of tasks: (1)
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Predicting</jats:italic>
                    inputs for specific execution features, guiding test generators and developers; (2)
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Replacing</jats:italic>
                    the original program during search-based testing or fuzzing, reducing costly or risky executions; (3) Predicting which program parts a test input will execute, guiding
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">test selection</jats:italic>
                    ; (4) Predicting which input will trigger a specific behavior, serving as an
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">input filter</jats:italic>
                    to prevent undesired outcomes. To our knowledge, this is the first work that trains reversible, program-specific neural machine translation models to both predict execution behavior from inputs and synthesize inputs to achieve the requested behavior in real-world programs.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    In our evaluation of real-world programs, including
                    <jats:monospace>Bottle</jats:monospace>
                    and the Google
                    <jats:monospace>re2</jats:monospace>
                    library, we show that neural program modeling can predict execution features for unseen inputs, achieving similarity ratios ranging from 91.57% to 98.59%. We can also predict program inputs that trigger specified behaviors with accuracy and recall up to 100% after validation and refinement. All predictions can be automatically validated and refined, either by retraining the model on new input-trace pairs or by using a backpropagation loop to adjust its parameters. Model training and inference are resource-efficient and can be performed on commodity hardware.
                  </jats:p>
title: Neural Program Modeling Learning Program-Specific Models that Predict Execution Features from Input Features and vice versa
